newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-UEFA ATTEMPT TO DEFLECT JOHANSSON CRITICISM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UEFA ATTEMPT TO DEFLECT JOHANSSON CRITICISM.

text.p: UEFA released a statement on Friday expressing "surprise and concern" at the interpretation of controversial remarks made by president Lennart Johansson in a Swedish newspaper article.
In an attempt to limit the damage caused by Johansson's reported references to Africans as "blackies", UEFA stressed the president's "great admiration for African football."
"The Africans are friends of mine," said Johansson in the statement. "I said in the interview, I love their way of playing the game.
"In Europe we can learn a lot from the African players and I think it can be such a valuable experience for us to meet them at all levels.
"But I also think that we can do some things which will be helpful for them and thereby further improve African football."
The statement also made note of Johansson's support for African leaders, notably Issa Hayatou, his counterpart as head of the African Football Confederation and the African players.
Nowhere in the statement, however, did Johansson deny or apologise for his comments. Earlier the 67-year-old Swede had admitted to a Swedish newspaper he had been quoted correctly.
